spine_row.acip: 'DI LA KUN SLONG BYE BRAG CAN DPER NA, LHAS BYIN KHO NA BSAD SNYAM NAS SBYOR BA BRTZAMS PA NA MCHOD SBYIN DU NOR NAS BSAD NA, DNGOS GZHI'I SDIG MED PAS DE LTA BU LA 'DU SHES MA 'KHRUL BA DGOS SHING , SBYOR BA'I DUS SU GANG BYUNG YANG GSOD SNYAM PA KUN SLONG SPYI LA ZHUGS PA YOD NA 'DU SHES MA 'KHRUL BA MI DGOS SO, , TSUL 'DI NI LHAG MA DGU LA YANG CI RIGS PAR SHES PAR BYA'O, ,
spine_row.wylie: 'di la kun slong bye brag can dper na, lhas byin kho na bsad snyam nas sbyor ba brtsams pa na mchod sbyin du nor nas bsad na, dngos gzhi'i sdig med pas de lta bu la 'du shes ma 'khrul ba dgos shing , sbyor ba'i dus su gang byung yang gsod snyam pa kun slong spyi la zhugs pa yod na 'du shes ma 'khrul ba mi dgos so, , tshul 'di ni lhag ma dgu la yang ci rigs par shes par bya'o,
spine_row.english: This is a particular feature of the motivation. Suppose, for example, that you think to yourself, "I only want to kill John," and undertake the deed. Then you mistake Joe for John, and kill Joe. In this sort of case, there is no "actual- commission" stage; so we can see that, for this stage, the conception you have must be unmistaken. If on the other hand you undertake the deed with some general kind of motivation, if you think to yourself, "I'll kill anyone I happen to meet," then this detail of the conception having to be unmistaken need not be complete. You should understand that this point applies to the other nine as well.

spine_row.wylie: srog gcod pa ni bsams bzhin du, ,ma nor bar ni gzhan gsad pa'o, ,ma byin len pa gzhan gyi nor, ,gathu dang 'jab bus bdag gir byed
spine_row.english: Taking life is killing another being Purposely, and without a mistake. Stealing is to take possession of Another's wealth by means of force or stealth. "What," one may ask, "is the basic nature of each of the ten non-virtues?" (1) The taking of life is defined as killing another being purposely, and without a mistake.  The word "purposely" is meant to indicate that there is no fault where the being in question has died but there was no intent. The words "without a mistake" are meant to indicate that no "actual-commission" stage of an act occurs in a case of mistaken identity; for example, in a case where you undertake to kill Devadatta but instead kill Yajana because you have mistaken him for Devadatta.  The word "another," finally, is meant to indicate that no "actual-commission" stage occurs either in an instance where one takes his own life. (2) Stealing is to take possession of another's wealth, purposely and without a mistake, whether it be by means of superior force of by stealth-                -undetected.
